mcqs.question: Let A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {3, 2, 1}. Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: A and B are equal sets.
options.B: A is a proper subset of B.
options.C: A and B are disjoint sets.
options.D: A and B have no elements in common.

mcqs.answer: A and B are equal sets.
mcqs.explanation: Two sets are equal if they contain exactly the same elements, irrespective of order. Both A and B contain 1, 2 and 3, so they are equal. Option B is false because a set cannot be a proper subset of another set that has the same elements. Options C and D are false because the sets share all their elements.

mcqs.question: Class X has 25 students and Class Y also has 25 students, but the names of the students are different. Which description best fits the relationship between the two sets of students?

options.A: The two sets are equal sets.
options.B: The two sets are equivalent sets.
options.C: One set is a subset of the other.

mcqs.answer: The two sets are equivalent sets.
mcqs.explanation: Equivalent sets are sets that have the same number of elements (same cardinality), even if the actual elements differ. Here both classes have 25 students, so they are equivalent. They are not equal because the members differ (Option A). Neither is a subset of the other (Option C) and they are not disjoint (Option D).

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the empty set?

options.A: A set that contains no elements, denoted by {} or ∅.
options.B: A set that contains the number zero as its only element.
options.C: A set that contains exactly one element, namely the empty set itself.
options.D: A set that contains all natural numbers.

mcqs.answer: A set that contains no elements, denoted by {} or ∅.
mcqs.explanation: The empty set is the unique set with no elements; it is represented by {} or the symbol ∅. Option B describes a singleton set {0}. Option C is a set with one element (the empty set), not the empty set itself. Option D describes an infinite set, not the empty set.

mcqs.question: A set is called finite if:

options.A: Its elements can be listed completely in a limited number of steps.
options.D: It contains itself as an element.

mcqs.answer: Its elements can be listed completely in a limited number of steps.
mcqs.explanation: A finite set has a countable number of elements that can be enumerated in a finite amount of time. Option B describes an infinite set. Option C is a special case of a finite set (a singleton) but does not capture the general definition. Option D is not a property of finiteness.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly characterises an infinite set?

options.A: It can be placed in one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself.
options.B: It contains a finite number of elements.
options.D: It contains only the empty set as its element.

mcqs.answer: It can be placed in one‑to‑one correspondence with a proper subset of itself.
mcqs.explanation: An infinite set is one that can be put into a bijection with a proper subset of itself (e.g., natural numbers and even numbers). Options B and C describe finite sets. Option D describes a singleton set containing the empty set, not an infinite set.

mcqs.question: A singleton set is:

options.A: A set containing exactly one element.
options.C: A set containing infinitely many elements.
options.D: A set containing exactly two elements.

mcqs.answer: A set containing exactly one element.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a singleton set has precisely one element. Option B is the empty set. Option C describes an infinite set. Option D describes a set with two elements, not a singleton.

mcqs.question: If X = {a, b, c} and Y = {c, b, a}, which statement is correct?

options.A: X and Y are equal sets.
options.B: X is a proper subset of Y.
options.C: X and Y are disjoint sets.
options.D: X has more elements than Y.

mcqs.answer: X and Y are equal sets.
mcqs.explanation: Equality of sets depends only on having exactly the same elements, not on order. Both X and Y contain a, b, and c, so they are equal. The other options are false because the sets are neither subsets nor disjoint, and they have the same number of elements.

mcqs.question: Consider P = {1,2,3,4} and Q = {a,b,c,d}. Which description best fits their relationship?

options.A: P and Q are equal sets.
options.B: P and Q are equivalent sets.
options.C: P is a subset of Q.
options.D: P and Q are disjoint sets.

mcqs.answer: P and Q are equivalent sets.
mcqs.explanation: Both sets have four elements, so they have the same cardinality and are equivalent. They are not equal because their elements differ (Option A). Neither is a subset of the other (Option C), and they share no common elements, making them disjoint, but the more precise relationship concerning size is equivalence (Option D is true but less specific; the question asks for the best description, which is equivalence).
